title: The dog at the threshold
hookLine: they sleep for years with their dog stretched at the entrance (18:18, 18:25)

lines: THE SUN SWINGS PAST THE OPENING.
cards: The young men have prayed, and now they sleep. Inside, the cave is dim. The sun, the surah says, swings past the opening, to the right in the morning and the left in the evening, so it never falls full on them.
Someone looking in would swear they were awake. And lying across the entrance, front legs stretched out on the threshold, is a dog. The Qur'an tells you exactly where it lies.

teach.b: Verse eighteen ends, in Pickthall's words: "and their dog stretching out his paws on the threshold." Al-wasid, the threshold, the open ground at the mouth of the cave: where a guard would lie.
In the same verse, God turns the sleepers to the right and the left, while the dog stays put. A few verses on, the story does something unusual. People argue about how many sleepers there were.
Some will say three, their dog the fourth. Some say five, their dog the sixth, guessing at the unseen. Some say seven, and their dog the eighth.
And the verse ends: say, my Lord knows best their number. Nobody's count leaves out the dog. The men are a number in dispute; the dog is in every version.

teach.h: THREE, FIVE OR SEVEN, PLUS THE DOG.
teach.b: Verse twenty-five gives a length for the sleep, three hundred years and nine more, and the next verse adds that God knows best how long they stayed.
And the animal that followed them in is remembered in a surah recited on Fridays. A hadith in Bukhari fits beside it. A man on a hot road found a dog panting and licking the dirt from thirst.
He climbed down a well, filled his leather sock with water, held it in his teeth to climb back up, and gave the dog a drink. God thanked him and forgave him.
The companions asked: is there reward for us even with animals? The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said: in every living, breathing creature there is reward.
Muslim schools of law differ about dogs, their purity and keeping them in the house. On kindness to them, the hadith is plain.

how: Muslims cite the hadith of the man who watered a thirsty dog when teaching kindness to animals; schools of law differ on the ritual purity of dogs and on keeping them indoors.

o: the threshold at the mouth of the cave
the stone that sealed the cave shut
the dog that guarded the young men

games.q: it's a hot road. you've just drunk from a well, and you see a dog licking the dirt from thirst. you have no bucket. what does the man in the hadith do?
o: climb back down and bring up water in his leather sock, held in his teeth.
call someone else to deal with it.
games.why: he filled his sock, held it in his teeth to climb, and gave the dog a drink. God thanked him and forgave him (Bukhari).

practice: Bring to mind an animal you know: a neighbor's dog, a cat on a wall, the pigeons at the bus stop.
Picture what it needs, water on a hot day, shade, someone not shooing it, and one small, safe kindness that would meet that need; a bowl of water by the door counts.

wordCard.voice: Al-wasid. The threshold where the sleepers' dog stretched its paws, and stayed counted in every version of the story. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: and their dog stretching out its forelegs at the threshold (18:18).

carryVoice: Your line: even the dog is remembered. Every count includes it. That's day four hundred sixty-five.
